reviewed_facts: Original input and gate-prefix values are reused only before the replaced gate. Every later gate is replayed with the original selectors and operation, including reconvergent uses.
Target flags are defined from the original trace: target_here AND NOT seen_target, so exactly the earliest exact target is tested. target_before_flags[g] exempts replacements after that target.

Replacing AND by either operand can only increase values; negative_gain is required. Replacing OR by an operand can only decrease values; positive_loss is required. Gate operation true means AND, matching the clauses.
Replacing a gate by false requires loss of a required positive; replacement by true requires gain of a required negative.
Changed-value tests use graph edge rows and all maximal-independent-set rows, so absence of change on every separating row implies exact graph correctness for the monotone replacement.
CNF bool literal handling uses type checks/identity before integer negation. Later replay operands are fresh variables; constant replacements are used through selected-wire equality constraints.
Post-model replay independently recomputes all later gates up to first_target_gate and checks the corresponding signed loss/gain for every replacement.
scope: Necessary cuts for globally minimum nonconstant exact graph circuits, using separately reviewed constant/alias simplification. They are not justified for a minimum restricted nonstar subclass; a preserving simplification may change ownership/profile. No SAT or Lean run was performed.
